name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.167.0 — replay --select now skips any candidate review run already named by a pristine-red setup-failed replay row — a standing claim that the target's tree cannot be rebuilt into the state its CLEAN review judged (a close-time expiry sweep deleting a test the review's own coverage leg counted is the recorded cause). Such rows record no measurement and so never advance the dueness window; without the skip the same unreproducible target was re-picked on every run, burning a full setup cycle each time and leaving the harness due forever. When every candidate in the window is so claimed, --select refuses with its own named exit-1 message rather than the generic no-eligible-row one. 7.166.0 — A whole-product note now blocks the final sign-off instead of every journey. A journey's approve control counts only the questions and notes raised on that journey's own screens, so a product-wide doubt no longer makes every journey unapprovable; when a journey is clean while product-wide notes remain, the review page says how many still block sign-off, and `--mark approved` refuses by name until they are answered. Recorded as ADR-0019. 7.165.0 — The journey review page answers to a design: design/chrome-mocks/review.html is the binding reference artifact, cited as design_source. The rail's Whole project count is derived server-side instead of looked up in a map that could never hold it, so the first paint, a ?clean render and a capture all carry the number the browser re-derives. The scope band states its scope as real DOM text rather than CSS generated content, five .rv-* utilities win back the cascade from the generic .rv button rule, and the composer's dead scope toggle is deleted. Tests pin the page again, this time opt-in so they outlive the spec's close.
